# Site Administration
The senior employee on site runs the Company's operation on the colony. These are their tools and their obligations.
## The Corporate Affairs Console The console is restricted to grade WYC5 and above. - [bold]Treasury[/bold]: the corporate budget. Withdrawals are taxed by the colony at its current income tax rate. - [bold]Transit tariff[/bold]: the Company's cut of every submission the colony ships out, up to 50%. Changes are announced to the colony. - [bold]Corporate support[/bold]: calls in Company security, synthetics or contractors, paid from the corporate budget. - [bold]Contracts[/bold]: the site lease, licences, loans, work orders and divestment (see [textlink="Colonial Partnership" link="CMUHandbookExecutivePartnership"/]).
## Corporate Support Support is paid from the corporate budget and arrives by shuttle. Each request must be justified in writing afterwards. - [bold]Corporate Security Team[/bold]: a Security Sergeant and three officers with rifles, tasers and restraints, to reinforce the site's own guards. - [bold]Riot Control Team[/bold]: PMC Dispatch's crowd-control contractors, a team leader, four Crowd Control Specialists and a grenadier, all with non-lethal weapons and gas masks. For colonists who have turned on Company property. - [bold]Internal Affairs Team[/bold]: a senior auditor and an auditor from the Directorate's Office of Internal Affairs, with a Personal Protection detail of a specialist and two officers. They audit the site's records, accounts and staff, and may relieve staff of duty. They report to head office, not to whoever called them. - [bold]Asset Recovery Team[/bold]: PMC Dispatch's retrieval contractors, a team leader, two operators, a retrieval technician and a medic, with a specimen crate on their shuttle. For anything the site has lost or had taken: data, a specimen or a person. - [bold]Biohazard Containment Unit[/bold]: PMC Dispatch's sterilisation crew in sealed bio suits, a team leader, two incinerator specialists, a containment technician and a medic. For contamination the site can't hold. They destroy the hazard; Hazard Transport moves it. - [bold]Hazard Transport[/bold]: a liaison, two scientists and two guards to collect or deliver research material. - [bold]IPIE legal team[/bold]: a synthetic Company lawyer and a protection officer, for legal and investigative work. - [bold]PMC contractors[/bold]: a full PMC fireteam. Expensive, and for situations that are already beyond site security. - [bold]Working Joes[/bold]: synthetic labour.
## The Budget - The budget is earned by office terminal work, research, trade and the Company's colonial contracts. - Office staff are to be kept at the work terminals when they have no other task. - Cash paid into the console counts as budget but not as earnings. The Company's share price follows what the site earns, not what is deposited.
## The Markets - Office staff trade goods and commodities on the Company's account. The site may hold no more than $10,000 in goods at once, and positions aren't carried over when the site's books close. - The Company's newswire reports market news before the market reacts. Colonists trading from personal desktops only hear it moments before the move. - The Company does not trade stock from site terminals. Colonists can, and they trade Weyland-Yutani. - The Company's share price follows the site. Profit lifts it. News of the first Company casualties knocks it down. Personnel lost beyond revival in large numbers, a lost research licence or a divestment sends it down hard, and the Company's rivals move in when it falls. Head office reads the share price.
## Research - Research is the Company's main source of value on any colony, and depends on the colony's research licence. - The executive is responsible for keeping the licence. Losing it is reported to head office and recorded against the executive. - The Lead Researcher reports to the senior employee. What the laboratory is really working on is covered in [textlink="Research Programmes" link="CMUHandbookExecutiveResearch"/].
## Staff - The senior employee settles disputes between departments. Their decision is final until someone more senior arrives. - Disciplinary matters are recorded and passed to head office. Staff are not dismissed on site. - Corporate Security answers to the senior employee through the Security Sergeant.
## Reporting - Significant events are reported up the chain in writing. Losses are reported promptly and successes immediately. - Reports that could expose the Company go to Communications before anyone else, and go nowhere else.
